summary: Klamath County cupola lookout built on Old Baldy in 1924 and gone by 1961. No source describes what, if anything, remains at the site today.

facts.status_note: Removed, destroyed or burned in 1961, depending on the source

events.note: Cupola lookout house on an enclosed tower of about ten feet, replacing a lookout tree on Brush Mountain
Stan Peterson stationed there for summer 1924 (Medford Mail Tribune item quoted on Rex's page)
Men from a South Fork of the Rogue CCC camp sent to Old Baldy to act as lookouts (Medford Mail Tribune item)
Register says removed; firelookout.com says destroyed; Rex's page says it burned, no longer needed

corrections.why: The only 'D-6' in the sources is an October 1925 item that refers to a 'Who's Who' column. It is not a lookout design. The register and firelookout.com give no design code, so the design value should be removed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the cupola cabin was removed in 1961, firelookout.com says destroyed, and Rex's page says it burned because it was no longer needed. All three are recorded.
Papers quoted on Rex's page name Stan Peterson (June 1924), Dan Pederson (September 1924) and Dan Peterson (October 1925). The sources do not show whether these are the same man.

notes_for_editor: Do not use https://www.oregonhikers.org/field_guide/Old_Baldy_Hike for this record. It describes a different Old Baldy in the Mt. Hood National Forest (Salmon-Huckleberry Wilderness, near Githens Mountain) and was excluded. Access and present-day status are not described by any source, so no access fact is recorded. Brief's design D-6 is treated as a misreading of a column name. The story is about 215 words. The lookout's name is spelled three ways in the quoted papers; the story reports this rather than choosing one.
